Strictly diagonally dominant: |aᵢᵢ| > Σ_{j≠i} |aᵢⱼ| in every row. Then Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel converge for any starting vector.
Jacobi: xᵢ⁽ᵏ⁺¹⁾ = (bᵢ − Σ_{j≠i} aᵢⱼxⱼ⁽ᵏ⁾)/aᵢᵢ: every component uses the OLD vector.
Gauss–Seidel: same formula but uses each NEW component as soon as it is computed; usually converges faster. Memory trick Jacobi = all old values; Gauss–Seidel = newest values immediately.
SOR: Gauss–Seidel with a relaxation factor ω (1 < ω < 2 over-relaxes to speed convergence; ω = 1 is Gauss–Seidel).
